subject: StoneMill security questionnaire: hosted API data geography, retention, and deletion
messages:
From: Joanne Lee <joanne.lee@stonemillhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: StoneMill Security <security@stonemillhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API: data geography, retention & deletion questions

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the Hosted API walkthrough last week. Security asked me to send a short set of clarifying questions so we can complete our vendor review. We bundled the items in the attached PDF but I pasted the key points below to keep the thread short. Could you confirm the behavior for your hosted offering (not Dedicated/Private) and any contractual options?

1) Data geography: can we ensure request payloads and derived data stay in a US region only (no cross-region failover)? If not by default, what controls exist?

2) Retention defaults: what are the default retention windows for raw request payloads, logs, caching (KV cache), and aggregated metrics? Are these configurable per-tenant?

3) Deletion/erasure: if we submit a data deletion request for a tenant, what is the end-to-end timeline until data is fully purged from active stores and backups? Does deletion cascade to observability traces, audit logs, and backups?

4) Backups/snapshots: do backups contain decrypted customer payloads? What is the backup retention window and how is deletion handled for long-term snapshots?

5) Cryptography: do you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for hosted customers? If so, what key lifecycle guarantees are there when a tenant requests deletion?

6) Evidence: can you provide a short summary of where to find the SOC2 report and any whitepaper that documents the hosted data lifecycle?

We'd like short, concrete answers we can paste into our questionnaire. If it helps, we can hop on a 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Joanne
Senior InfoSec Analyst
StoneMill Health

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API: data geography, retention & deletion questions

Hi Joanne —

Appreciate the clear list. Below are concise, copy-paste friendly answers for StoneMill's questionnaire. I've put the short answers first and a single-line expanded note where helpful. Happy to jump on a call if you'd like us to walk this through with your team.

1) Data geography (short): Yes — Hosted API supports strict regional routing for customer traffic; you can restrict to a single US region (us-west-2 or us-east-1) via tenant routing controls.
- Note: In the strict routing configuration we do not perform cross-region automatic failover for customer request payloads. Fallbacks for infra-level health are limited to control-plane metadata only and are subject to customer opt-in.

2) Retention defaults (short): Default retention windows for Hosted API: raw request payloads 45 days (configurable 0–365), KV cache TTL 24 hours (ephemeral), request/interaction logs 90 days, aggregated metrics 365 days.
- Note: Enterprise agreements can set custom retention ceilings and defaults per tenant (e.g., reduce payload retention to 0–7 days).

3) Deletion/erasure (short): Active datastore removal: within 24 hours of request; observability/audit logs: scrubbed/hashed within 72 hours where practical; backups/snapshots: removed at next backup cycle (see #4).
- Note: Deletion requests initiate an automated workflow: (a) mark objects for deletion and scrub from active indexes, (b) rotate caches and invalidate KV entries, (c) schedule purge from analytics pipelines, and (d) submit for backup retention removal. We supply a confirmation when the active purge completes.

4) Backups/snapshots (short): Backups may contain encrypted customer payloads. Default backup rotation policy (hosted): daily incremental backups with a 30-day retention window for short-term snapshots and a separate long-term snapshot store (if enabled) with explicit retention. Purge from backups occurs on next retention-aware cleanup; for daily backups this is typically within 72 hours but may be up to 30 days for long-term snapshots unless contractually shortened.
- Note: We can include contractual SLAs for backup purge windows for enterprise customers. Backups use envelope encryption; if customer-managed keys are used and keys are destroyed after a deletion request, recovered data becomes unreadable (crypto-erase).

5) Cryptography (short): Yes — customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported for hosted customers via our KMS integrations.
- Note: With BYOK, Redwood stores encrypted blobs and does not retain plaintext keys. A key-rotation or key-destruction workflow will render backups inaccessible (crypto-erase). We provide guidance and operational support for key lifecycle events.

6) Evidence (short): SOC 2 report and hosted-data lifecycle whitepaper: https://redwood.ai/soc2-report-link and https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-data-lifecycle

If you'd like, we can produce short, question-specific statements suitable for inclusion directly in StoneMill's questionnaire table. Would you like that as a follow-up?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: data geography, retention & deletion questions

Thanks Tessa — that's helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our infra team before we mark this complete: 

A) For backups: you mentioned daily incremental backups + long-term snapshots. Can you confirm whether the incremental backups contain decrypted request payloads at rest, or are they always stored encrypted? If encrypted, are those backups accessible using Redwood-managed keys by your ops team?

B) Deletion timeline: you say "active datastore removal within 24 hours" and backup purge at next rotation. We need to understand the maximum window we should communicate to our legal team if we aim for a contract clause that requires purging of customer data from all Redwood-managed storage within 30 days. Is that feasible?

C) Observability traces: do your retention/erasure controls apply uniformly to X-ray/tracing data and to vendor-provided observability (e.g., third-party logging sinks)? Can we opt-out of sending traces containing PII to external SaaS sinks?

D) Audit evidence: for deletion confirmation, can you provide a certificate or assertive statement (signed letter) that confirms the purge step completed for a given tenant?

If you prefer, Hannah and Neha can be looped into the call to go deeper on technical and contractual options.

— StoneMill Security
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: StoneMill Security <security@stonemillhealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Joanne Lee <joanne.lee@stonemillhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: data geography, retention & deletion questions

Hi — thanks for the great follow-ups. Short answers below and next steps at the end.

A) Backups encryption and ops access: All backups are encrypted at rest. By default backups are encrypted with Redwood-managed envelope keys; the underlying backup files remain encrypted. Our ops team cannot decrypt without access to the envelope keys. For customers using BYOK, the customer-managed key wraps the envelope key and Redwood does not have access to the plaintext customer key. In practice: (a) backups are encrypted at rest, (b) ops-level access to decrypted payloads is limited and audited, and (c) BYOK customers gain an additional control surface (see crypto-erase).

B) Contractual purge within 30 days: Feasible — we can agree to a 30-day maximum end-to-end purge for Hosted API in enterprise contracts. Operationally that would include: immediate active datastore purge within 24 hours, observability/audit trace scrub/hashing within 72 hours, and backup/snapshot removal within 30 days (backup rotation cleanup). We will add language that allows shorter windows where required and outline any exceptions (e.g., legal hold).

C) Observability traces and third-party sinks: Traces that traverse Redwood's internal observability are covered by our retention controls; by default some traces and debug logs are captured for 90 days. For third-party sinks: you may opt out of forwarding data to external SaaS sinks via tenant-level routing rules; we recommend enabling PII-redaction rules or disabling trace forwarding for sensitive tenants.

D) Deletion confirmation / attestation: We can provide a deletion confirmation report for each purge request (automated PDF) showing objects queued/removed and timestamps. For higher assurance we offer a signed attestation addendum as part of our enterprise package.

Next steps: (1) If StoneMill wants the 30-day contractual purge window, we'll route this to Legal & Contracts and provide the precise clause language. (2) If you want a brief call, Hannah (technical lead for retention & backups) and Neha (security lead for BYOK) are available Thurs/Fri this week — what time works for you?

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
